title: Synchronous shutdown / standby — quick comms & ops cheat sheet (scratch)
content:
Context: quick internal notes for a planned synchronous shutdown/standby window (short, controlled) — lightweight comms and ops checklist. This is a scratchpad: lots of placeholders and TODOs.

Summary (one line): We need a short, coordinated quiet window where select infra (api-gateway, routing layer, a small subset of replicas) enters standby for a config migration and kernel rollout. Target: 30–45 minute window, low-traffic hours. Aim is zero-data-loss and graceful degraded responses for hosted API customers.

Audience: on-call SREs, platform eng on-call, support leads, duty product PM.

Goals:
- Apply kernel/runtime change with minimal user-visible impact
- Validate rollback path within the window
- Keep customers informed if >5% error increase or latency SLO breach

Proposed window (draft):
- Date: Friday, 2025-02-28 (weekend buffer) — tentative
- Prep check-in: T-72h (ops checklist), T-24h confirm, T-2h final go/no-go
- Execute: 02:30–03:15 PT (low traffic region)
- Post-run validation: +30m monitoring and smoke tests

Owner & backups:
- Primary: Mae Park (me) — coordination, slack author
- Backup 1: Adrian Chen — rollback lead
- Backup 2: Priya Kumar — customer comms support

Services in scope (short list):
- api-gateway (ingress routing) — do a rolling config reload + small replica temporary pause
- model-serving-proxy (edge) — warm shutdown of a subset of instances
- worker-pool (batch tasks) — pause acceptance of new jobs
- logging-forwarder (non-blocking) — ensure persistence ongoing

Impact matrix (quick):
- Hosted API: transient 502/504 possible for <5 minutes per region during traffic drain; streaming may be interrupted (clients should reconnect)
- Dedicated customers: no-impact expected if pinned to isolated capacity (call out exceptions)
- Private: none — customers on private control plane unaffected (unless they opt-in)

Customer-facing blurb (short):
- "Planned infrastructure maintenance to improve runtime stability and roll out performance optimizations. Brief interruptions to API requests may occur between 02:30–03:15 PT; we will monitor and post an update when complete. If you experience an issue after the window, please open a support ticket and tag urgent."

Internal Slack announcement (short, post at T-30m):
- Channel: #ops-announce and #oncall
- Message draft: "PLANNED: short maintenance window starting in 30m (02:30 PT). Scoped to api-gateway + model-proxy. Expect short reconnections and transient 5xx while we drain traffic. Mae (primary) / Adrian (rollback). Pager teams on standby. Will post completion & post-mortem link."

Escalation & contacts (quick):
- Pager: Platform SRE rotation (pager flow: oncall -> duty lead -> eng manager)
- Urgent exec notify: Rowan (CTO) and Hana (Head of Ops) if >30m outage or SLA breach

Ops runbook (condensed steps) — annotate to expand before T-24h:
1) T-24h: confirm canary traffic split and rollback images are ready; snapshot routing rules (terraform state backup + manual note)
2) T-2h: disable scheduled batch jobs; ensure retention/backup for in-flight KV caches
3) T-15m: post pre-maint message in #ops-announce and #customer-ops (for support ops heads)
4) T-5m: start graceful drain on first N replicas (N=2) from edge; monitor 5xx and latency; if >3% 5xx in 5m -> abort
5) Execute kernel/config swap on drained hosts; bring back into pool after smoke tests (token generation, latency check, small synthetic prompt)
6) Repeat rolling for next batch until complete
7) Post-run: run integration smoke suite, check streaming reconnect behavior, verify billing events unchanged
8) Post-mortem: create a short incident doc (template) within 48h

Abort / rollback criteria (quick):
- Any sustained >5% 5xx over 10 minutes across majority of regions
- Streaming clients fail to reconnect after 10 minutes post-restart
- Persistent KV cache inconsistency detected (manual validation fails)

Support handoff script (for support leads):
- "Maintenance window ongoing. Known scope: api-gateway/model-proxy. If customer reports errors, ask for request-id + time-range and escalate to #oncall with tags. We will inform if workaround available; otherwise request ticket and mark as maintenance-impacted."

Anticipated Q&A (quick bullets):
Q: Will embeddings endpoints be affected?
A: Embeddings are hosted on dedicated pools — low likelihood. If embedding requests proxy through affected routing, customer may see reconnects; highlight region and customer setup in the support ticket.

Q: Do we have rollback images?
A: Yes — Adrian to verify image tags and keep a rollback checklist at T-2h. If rollback executed, expect ~10–15 min to restore full traffic.

Q: How will this affect our SLAs?
A: Small window and pre-notified; we will not proactively credit customers unless outage exceeds SLA thresholds. Support will triage on a case-by-case basis.

Draft follow-up posting (short) to #ops-announce after completion:
- "MAINTENANCE COMPLETE: Completed kernel rollout and config swap for api-gateway/model-proxy (02:30–03:12 PT). No active rollbacks. Monitoring for 30m. Post-mortem TBD; initial notes at <link>. Thanks to the oncall team: Mae, Adrian, Priya."

Open items / TODOs (my personal TODOs):
- [ ] Confirm exact replica counts and N for draining (ask release-eng)
- [ ] Finalize customer-facing email for any affected enterprise accounts (ask CS: Priya)
- [ ] Add synthetic streaming reconnect test to smoke suite (dev: Inez)
- [ ] Create post-mortem template link and prefill later
- [ ] Get timezone cross-check with APAC region leads (avoid overlap)

Notes to self: keep message short and calm; avoid technical jargon in customer-facing text. Use exact timestamps (ISO) in final comms. Remember to capture request-ids for any customer reports so we can tie to traces.

Scratch comments (random):
- If we can do a small canary (1% traffic) earlier in the day, it reduces risk. Might be possible if we reserve a dedicated canary pool.
- Consider adding a passive header FYI in responses (X-RI-Maintenance: 2025-02-28/02:30-03:15PT) so support can filter requests quickly. Need privacy/engineering review.

End of notes — will turn into a short ops doc and a concise Slack message once confirmed.
